properties.statement: `volatility: append_only` IS A PROPERTY OF THE FILE WHILE 'DOES THIS CHANGE CARRY DESIGN MEANING' IS A PROPERTY OF THE EDIT — SO A STRUCTURAL REWRITE INSIDE AN APPEND-ONLY ARTIFACT IS EXEMPTED SILENTLY. Reported by api-boss `5d608b85` (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-08), and the report opens by crediting the Stop hook for catching an omission of theirs. WHAT HAPPENED: they made 5 graph writes (a concurrency probe, created and deleted, net zero) and also edited `P.md`, a REGISTERED Artifact, changing a BINDING worker rule. They ran loop_status and it reported `undispositioned_drift: 0`. That zero means NO DETECTOR HAD LOOKED AT THE CHANGED FILE, not that the file was unchanged. The Stop hook — not loop_status — is what said 'file(s) changed this session with no ChangeEvent recorded'. They state plainly they would otherwise have finished the session believing the loop was clean. THE DESIGN ISSUE UNDERNEATH: `art:fleet_bus_p` carries `volatility: append_only`, which is correct and useful for a bus, where a routine post should not owe a drift disposition forever. But their edit was NOT an append — it was a structural rewrite of binding rules inside the same file. An append-only marker therefore exempts EVERY change to that file, including ones that move the design, and nothing anywhere reports that an exemption was applied. Today an exemption and a genuinely clean file look identical. FIX SHAPE: have append_only suppress drift REPORTING while still letting a caller record a `design_updated` disposition — or better, have the reconcile output say 'N artifacts exempted by volatility', so the exemption is visible rather than silent. WHAT THE LOOP BOUGHT THEM, reported because they expected bookkeeping and got a finding: propagate_change on the recorded event returned 55 impacted nodes and, at distance 3, a RISK CROSSING on `req:fleet_no_idle_worker` — their change inserts a mandatory orientation step between a worker being claimed and starting work, and the graph flagged the tension with the fleet's own never-idle requirement, which they had not considered and no reviewer had raised. They judged the tension acceptable but say they would not have known to make the judgement at all. They also recorded the disposition properly via set_artifact_checksum(design_updated, chg:...) and called the refusal-to-accept-silently good design that should be kept.
